title: Commitment Bundles Intake & SLA Mapping Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a repeatable intake, prioritization, and SLA-mapping process for customer requests that involve commitment bundles, invoicing structure changes, and marketplace crediting. This playbook is focused on non-bug commercial requests (contract changes, custom billing, tiered commitments, marketplace offsets). Goals: 1) Triage consistently so legal/finance/engineering effort estimates are accurate; 2) Surface cost-allocation implications and bookkeeping signals early; 3) Map commitment requests to an SLA/engagement tier and recommended product changes (billing-only vs. product+billing). Scope: - New commitment bundle structures (e.g., per-seat + reserved throughput hybrid) - One-off invoice formats and tagging rules for marketplace offsets - Conversion flows from promo/trial credits into committed credits - Billing reconciliation automation requests Out of scope: refunds, pure chargeback bugs, tax/VAT policy changes.
intake_flow: 1) Customer or AE submits a standardized 'Commitment Intake Form' (Confluence template link below). 2) PM on-call reviews within 48 hours and assigns initial priority lane: Enterprise, High Touch, or Self-Serve. 3) Finance and Legal receive auto-notification for anything tagged 'contract change' or 'invoice schema' and must add commentary within 5 business days. 4) PM produces a short 'feasibility & impact' memo (one page) and routes to ENG Product Ops for engineering estimate and to Billing Ops for process estimate. 5) Triage board meeting (twice weekly) ratifies roadmap placement and assigns owner for implementation or policy enforcement.
scoring_rubric: Score each request 0-100 across four axes: Customer Revenue Impact (0-40), Engineering Effort (0-25, inverted), Time-to-Value for Customer (0-20), Operational Risk/Complexity (0-15, inverted). Thresholds: >=70 => P0/Enterprise lane (requires SLA mapping and dedicated engineering commit); 50-69 => P1/High Touch (may be solved via config or scripts); <50 => P2/P3 or documented policy response. Use quantitative inputs: expected ARR uplift (use multiplier for logo expansion), estimated engineering days, manual ops hours per month, and whether marketplace credits change ledger flows.
sla_mapping_guidelines: If a request requires changes to model routing, dedicated capacity, or reserved pools, map to 'Dedicated SLA' and consult infra for latency/throughput SLO changes. If request is purely invoice schema, map to 'Billing Ops SLA' with 5 business day turnaround for templated changes or 15 business days for schema + integration changes. For marketplace crediting affecting revenue recognition, escalate to Finance/Revenue Ops for month-end compatibility and map to 'Finance SLA' with a 10 business day review. Include recommended default SLAs and escalation contacts in the final decision.
decision_tradeoffs: We evaluated three approaches for ex-post billing changes: 1) Manual billing adjustments via Finance (fastest but high ops cost), 2) Parameterized invoice templates + automation (medium upfront dev cost, low ops cost long term), 3) Product-level commitment primitives (largest engineering investment, best long-term signals for product analytics). Recommendation: default to (2) for most requests; reserve (3) for enterprise customers where revenue and product alignment justify multi-quarter work. Trade-offs include slower velocity for (3) and potential short-term ops burden for (1).
